<reason>Side B built the cleaner comparative route: the choice is not displacement versus stability, but localized, cushionable displacement from new supply versus corridor-wide bidding-up of scarce existing rentals after transit investment. Side A pressed compensation timing and signaling effectively, but its answer depended on conditional mandates plus rent stabilization and building mainly on nonresidential lots; Side B showed that can freeze occupied parcels, protect only incumbents, and preserve the scarcity that makes relocation and access harder. B also answered the by-right definition pressure by distinguishing objective pre-demolition standards from discretionary vetoes.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The decisive exchange was B's closing use of A's admissions: owners not selling is "the point," yet relying on parking lots and stabilization leaves movers locked out and manufactures the vacancy scarcity A blamed for voucher failure.</best_rebuttal>
